sources.title: Richard S. Sutton and Andrew G. Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction, second-edition draft
sources.locator: Full 455-page Stanford-hosted second-edition draft; §§13.1–13.6, printed pp. 266–276.

contents.name: Episodic policy-gradient theorem and its complete state-value recursion proof, equation (13.5)
Conversion of the episodic gradient to sampled returns; equation (13.6) and pseudocode include the factor gamma to the time index
The state-baseline identity, equation (13.8), and discounted REINFORCE-with-baseline update, equation (13.9)
One-step episodic actor-critic pseudocode and the distinction between baseline use and bootstrapping bias
Continuing average-reward policy-gradient variant requires an existing start-independent steady-state distribution under an ergodicity premise
General convergence claims for nonlinear or deep actor-critic updates
contents.reason: The assigned scope makes no such convergence claim; the source section supplies an algorithm and bias discussion, not a general deep-optimizer convergence theorem.

sources.title: Ronald J. Williams, Simple Statistical Gradient-Following Algorithms for Connectionist Reinforcement Learning, Machine Learning 8 (1992)
sources.locator: Complete 28-page article; §§2, 4–5 and Appendix A.1–A.2, printed pp. 230–238 and PDF pp. 249–253.

contents.name: Parameterized stochastic output distributions and the differentiability requirement
The score-function identity for REINFORCE and a baseline conditionally independent of the sampled output, Theorem 1 and Appendix A.1
Episodic REINFORCE through time-unfolding with shared parameters, Theorem 2 and Appendix A.2
Actor-critic combines an immediate-reinforcement learner with a temporal-difference critic
The source's scope warning that it has no general convergence theory for the full REINFORCE algorithm class
A discounted-time factor for the finite-MDP return convention used in this batch
contents.reason: Williams analyzes total episodic reinforcement in the cited result; the gamma-to-time factor is read in Sutton and Barto and proved locally for the current discounted-return definition.
